data.narrative:
Corintis is a Series A semiconductor company that has raised $25M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of eight private peers and three public semiconductor firms, anchoring on stage-matched private companies in the same sector.

Two triangulation methods yield applicable results. The stage-progression approach, applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $25M raised proxy, implies a $50M valuation. The peer-median method references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers—Rebellions ($2.3B Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B Series A), and Positron AI ($1.0B Series B)—yielding a $2.0B median valuation with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied; the target's revenue is not disclosed, which precludes applying the sector's 18.9x P/S median across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD.

The triangulated range spans $42.5M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.0B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around Corintis's positioning relative to established Series A peers. Stage-progression suggests a more conservative floor, while peer median reflects valuations of well-capitalized chip design startups in an active funding environment. Key sensitivities include technology differentiation relative to named peers, path to revenue, and customer adoption timelines—factors not quantifiable in this dataset.
